stem: An S3 landing zone for a data lake is queried heavily by date range, and the ingestion job currently writes every day's files into one flat prefix with no structure. Which TWO configuration changes would improve query pruning for two different parts of the pipeline? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Increase the number of Kinesis Data Streams shards feeding the landing zone
Lower the Firehose buffer size to deliver files faster
Write the landing-zone objects into a year/month/day partition scheme
Convert the existing Athena table to matching Hive-style partition keys
Enable S3 Intelligent-Tiering on the landing-zone bucket

rationale: Writing objects into a year/month/day partition scheme, and defining the Athena table with matching Hive-style partition keys, together let a date-range query prune everything outside the requested partitions instead of scanning the whole dataset. Adding more Kinesis Data Streams shards increases ingest throughput capacity but has no effect on how the resulting files are organized in S3 or how a query prunes them. Lowering the Firehose buffer size delivers more, smaller files sooner; it adds no partition structure. S3 Intelligent-Tiering moves objects between storage cost tiers based on access patterns, it has no effect on query pruning.
